Metric Definitions

The following metrics are used to evaluate coil optimization submissions:

Notation

The following notation is used throughout the mathematical definitions:

  • \(C_i\) denotes coil curve \(i\)

  • \(S\) denotes the plasma surface

  • \(\mathbf{r}_i\) denotes a point on coil curve \(C_i\)

  • \(\mathbf{s}\) denotes a point on the plasma surface \(S\)

  • \(\ell_i\) denotes arclength along coil curve \(C_i\)

  • \(L_i\) denotes the total length of coil curve \(C_i\)

  • \(\kappa_i\) denotes curvature along coil curve \(C_i\)

  • \(\frac{d\vec{F}_i}{d\ell_i}\) denotes force per unit length on coil curve \(C_i\)

  • \(\frac{d\vec{T}_i}{d\ell_i}\) denotes torque per unit length on coil curve \(C_i\)

  • \(N\) denotes the number of coils

  • \(d\ell_i\) denotes the differential arclength element along coil curve \(C_i\)

  • \(ds\) denotes the differential surface area element on the plasma surface \(S\)

  • \(\mathbf{B}\) denotes the magnetic field vector

  • \(\mathbf{n}\) denotes the unit normal vector to the plasma surface

Field Quality Metrics

Average Normalized Normal Field Component (\(\bar{B}_n\))

Average of the absolute value of the normalized normal field component across the plasma surface.

Mathematical form:

\[B_n = \frac{|\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{n}|}{|\mathbf{B}|}\]
\[\bar{B}_n = \frac{\int_{S} |\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{n}| ds}{\int_{S} |\mathbf{B}| ds}\]

Units: dimensionless

Lower values indicate better field quality.

Maximum Normalized Normal Field Component (\(\max(B_n)\))

Maximum value of the normalized normal field component across the plasma surface.

Mathematical form:

\[B_n = \frac{|\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{n}|}{|\mathbf{B}|}\]
\[\max(B_n) = \max_{\mathbf{s} \in S} B_n(\mathbf{s})\]

Units: dimensionless

Lower values indicate better field quality.

Coil Geometry Metrics

Fourier Order (\(n\))

Order of the Fourier series representation used for coil curves.

Mathematical form:

\[\mathbf{r}(\phi) = \mathbf{a}_0 + \sum_{m=1}^{n} \left[\mathbf{a}_m \cos(m\phi) + \mathbf{b}_m \sin(m\phi)\right]\]

where \(\mathbf{a}_0\), \(\mathbf{a}_m\), and \(\mathbf{b}_m\) are Fourier coefficients and \(\phi\) is the parameterization angle.

Units: dimensionless

Higher orders allow more complex coil shapes but increase the number of optimization variables.

Arclength Variation (\(J\))

Variance of incremental arclength between coil segments.

Mathematical form:

\[J = \text{Var}(l_i)\]

where \(l_i\) is the average incremental arclength on interval \(I_i\) from a partition \(\{I_i\}_{i=1}^L\) of \([0,1]\).

Units: \(\text{m}^2\) (meters squared)

Lower values indicate more uniform spacing along coils, which is important for manufacturing and field quality.

Maximum Curvature (\(\kappa_\text{max}\))

Maximum curvature value across all coils.

Mathematical form:

\[\kappa_\text{max} = \max_{i=1,\ldots,N} \max_{\ell_i \in [0,L_i]} \kappa_i(\ell_i)\]

Units: \(\text{m}^{-1}\) (inverse meters)

Lower values indicate coils without extreme curvature regions.

Mean Squared Curvature (\(\text{MSC}\))

Mean squared curvature per coil, averaged across all coils.

Mathematical form:

\[J = \frac{1}{L_i} \int_{C_i} \kappa_i^2(\ell_i) ~d\ell_i\]
\[\text{MSC} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} J_i\]

where \(L_i\) is the total length of coil curve \(C_i\), \(\ell_i\) is the arclength along the curve, and \(\kappa_i\) is the curvature.

Units: \(\text{m}^{-2}\) (inverse meters squared)

This provides a smoother penalty than maximum curvature, encouraging overall smoothness rather than just avoiding extreme values.

Total Length (\(L\))

Total length of all coils.

Mathematical form:

\[L = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \int_{C_i} d\ell_i\]

Units: \(\text{m}\) (meters)

Shorter coils are generally preferred for reduced material costs and improved manufacturability.

Fourier Continuation (FC)

Sequence of Fourier orders used in continuation method. The optimization starts with a low-order representation, converges, then extends the solution to higher orders using the previous solution as initial condition. This helps achieve convergence for complex problems.

Format: comma-separated list of orders (e.g., “4,6,8” means optimization was performed at orders 4, 6, and 8 sequentially). If not used, the column shows “—“.

Number of Base Coils (\(N\))

Number of base coils before applying stellarator symmetry.

Units: dimensionless

Typical values: 4, 6, 8, 12. More coils allow more complex field shaping but increase computational cost.

Total Superconductor Length (\(L_{\text{SC}}\))

Total length of superconducting tape required at reactor scale, accounting for the number of turns in each coil’s winding pack.

Mathematical form:

\[L_{\text{SC}} = \frac{1}{1000} \sum_{i=1}^{N_{\text{coils}}} N_{\text{turns},i} \times L_{\text{reactor},i}\]

where \(N_{\text{turns},i} = \max(N_{F,i},\, N_{J_c,i})\) is the number of turns per coil (driven by force limits or REBCO critical-current limits, whichever is larger), and \(L_{\text{reactor},i}\) is the reactor-scale length of coil \(i\). The factor of 1/1000 converts from meters to kilometers.

Units: \(\text{km}\) (kilometers)

Lower values indicate more economical coil designs requiring less superconducting material. This is a derived reactor-scale metric that combines the winding-pack turn count with the scaled coil lengths.

Separation Metrics

Minimum Coil-to-Coil Distance (\(d_{cc}\))

Minimum distance between any two coils.

Mathematical form:

\[d_{cc} = \min_{i \neq j} \min_{\mathbf{r}_i \in C_i, \mathbf{r}_j \in C_j} \left\| \mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j \right\|_2\]

Units: \(\text{m}\) (meters)

Ensures coils maintain a safe separation distance to prevent collisions.

Minimum Coil-to-Surface Distance (\(d_{cs}\))

Minimum distance between any coil and the plasma surface.

Mathematical form:

\[d_{cs} = \min_{i} \min_{\mathbf{r}_i \in C_i, \mathbf{s} \in S} \left\| \mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{s} \right\|_2\]

Units: \(\text{m}\) (meters)

Ensures coils maintain a safe distance from the plasma surface.

Force and Torque Metrics

Maximum Force Magnitude (\(F_\text{max}\))

Maximum force magnitude across all coils.

Mathematical form:

\[F_\text{max} = \max_{i=1,\ldots,N} \max_{\ell_i \in [0,L_i]} \left|\frac{d\vec{F}_i}{d\ell_i}\right|\]

Units: \(\text{N}/\text{m}\) (Newtons per meter)

High forces indicate coils that may be difficult to support mechanically.

Maximum Torque Magnitude (\(\tau_\text{max}\))

Maximum torque magnitude across all coils.

Mathematical form:

\[\tau_\text{max} = \max_{i=1,\ldots,N} \max_{\ell_i \in [0,L_i]} \left|\frac{d\vec{T}_i}{d\ell_i}\right|\]

Units: \(\text{N}\) (Newtons)

High torques can lead to mechanical instability.

Topology Metrics

Linking Number (\(\text{LN}\))

Topological measure of how coils are linked together.

Mathematical form:

\[\text{LN} = \frac{1}{4\pi} \sum_{i \neq j} \oint_{C_i} \oint_{C_j} \frac{\left(\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j\right) \cdot \left(d\mathbf{r}_i \times d\mathbf{r}_j\right)}{\left|\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j\right|^3}\]

Units: dimensionless

This metric ensures coils maintain their topological structure during optimization.

Performance Metrics

Total Optimization Time (\(t\))

Total time required to complete the optimization.

Units: \(\text{s}\) (seconds)

Lower values indicate more efficient optimization algorithms or faster convergence.

Composite Score

The Score column is a single-number summary of reactor-scale engineering feasibility. It is computed in two stages.

Stage 1: Hard Constraints

Hard constraints are evaluated first. If any hard constraint is violated the score is set to 0 and the entry is marked FAIL (excluded from the main leaderboard). Missing metrics are skipped.

Two hard constraints apply a transform before comparison:

  • Coil-coil linking number — compared as \(|\text{LN}|\) (absolute value), since the linking number may be negative.

  • Max turns per coil — the element-wise maximum of the per-coil turn-count list is compared against the bound.

Stage 2: Soft Constraint Geometric Mean

For each soft constraint whose metric is available (and whose bound is non-zero), a margin exponent \(m_i\) is computed:

\[\begin{split}m_i = \begin{cases} 1 - \text{value}_i\,/\,\text{bound}_i & \text{value} \leq \text{bound} \;(\text{upper-bound constraint})\\[6pt] \text{value}_i\,/\,\text{bound}_i - 1 & \text{value} \geq \text{bound} \;(\text{lower-bound constraint}) \end{cases}\end{split}\]

Positive \(m_i\) = constraint satisfied with margin; negative = violated.

Two soft constraints apply a transform to the raw metric before the margin calculation:

  • RMS curvature — \(\sqrt{\text{MSC}}\) is used (square root of the mean-squared curvature) so the comparison is in m-1.

  • Arclength variation — \(\sqrt{\text{Var}}\) is used (square root of the variance) so the comparison is in m.

The composite score is the geometric mean of the individual exponential factors:

\[\text{Score} = \exp\!\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} m_i\right) = \left(\prod_{i=1}^{n} e^{m_i}\right)^{\!1/n}\]

where \(n\) is the number of soft constraints for which metrics were available.

Interpretation

Score = 0

Hard infeasibility (coils delinked from plasma, coils interlinked, winding packs overlap, or too many turns required).

0 < Score < 1

Feasible but one or more soft constraints violated on average.

Score = 1

All soft constraints met exactly on average.

Score > 1

All constraints satisfied with engineering margin.

Score = None

No soft-constraint metrics available (legacy or missing data).

Entries are sorted by composite score descending (higher is better). Legacy entries without a composite score fall back to score_primary (lower squared flux is better) and appear after scored entries.

Worked Example

Consider a reactor-scale design with:

  • avg \(B_n/|B|\) = 0.005, \(d_{cs}\) = 1.5 m, \(d_{cc}\) = 0.8 m, \(L\) = 200 m, \(\kappa_{\max}\) = 0.7, \(\sqrt{\text{MSC}}\) = 0.6, \(\sqrt{\text{Var}}\) = 0.4, \(L_{\text{SC}}\) = 50 km

\[\begin{split}m_1 &= 1 - 0.005/0.01 &&= 0.500 \\ m_2 &= 1.5/1.3 - 1 &&\approx 0.154 \\ m_3 &= 0.8/0.7 - 1 &&\approx 0.143 \\ m_4 &= 1 - 200/220 &&\approx 0.091 \\ m_5 &= 1 - 0.7/1.0 &&= 0.300 \\ m_6 &= 1 - 0.6/1.0 &&= 0.400 \\ m_7 &= 1 - 0.4/1.0 &&= 0.600 \\ m_8 &= 1 - 50/100 &&= 0.500\end{split}\]

Mean margin \(= (0.500 + 0.154 + 0.143 + 0.091 + 0.300 + 0.400 + 0.600 + 0.500)\,/\,8 \approx 0.336\).

Score \(= \exp(0.336) \approx\) 1.399 — all constraints satisfied with comfortable engineering margin.

Reactor-Scale Constraints

All submissions are scaled to the ARIES-CS reference reactor (minor radius \(a = 1.7\,\text{m}\), on-axis field \(B_0 = 5.7\,\text{T}\)) before engineering feasibility is assessed.

Winding-Pack Turn-Count Model

The simsopt optimiser models each coil as a single filamentary turn carrying the total current \(I\). In a real reactor the winding pack contains \(N_{\text{turns}}\) turns, each carrying \(I / N_{\text{turns}}\). We estimate the required number of turns from two independent criteria and take the element-wise maximum:

\[N_{\text{turns},\,i} = \max\!\bigl(N_{\text{turns},\,i}^{(\text{force})},\; N_{\text{turns},\,i}^{(J_c)}\bigr)\]

1. Force-based turns

With \(N\) turns the Lorentz force per unit length on each turn is

\[F_{\text{turn}} = \frac{F_{\text{reactor,single-turn}}}{N_{\text{turns}}}\]

For each coil we find the minimum \(N\) to keep \(F_{\text{turn}} \leq 0.5\,\text{MN/m}\):

\[N_{\text{turns},\,i}^{(\text{force})} = \left\lceil \frac{F_{\text{reactor},\,i}}{0.5\;\text{MN/m}} \right\rceil\]

2. Critical-current-density-based turns

This criterion ensures the HTS superconductor operates within its critical envelope. The model follows the Stellaris winding-pack design (Lion et al., Fusion Engineering and Design 214, 2025, 114868, Table 7–8 and Section 2.9).

REBCO tape-stack \(J_c\) model. A Kim-like parametrisation calibrated to tape-stack data at 20 K (field-aligned tapes):

\[J_c(B, T) = \frac{C_0}{1 + (B/B_0)^\alpha} \;\times\;\frac{1 - T/T_c}{1 - T_{\text{ref}}/T_c}\]

with fitted constants at \(T_{\text{ref}} = 20\,\text{K}\):

Parameter

Value

Description

\(C_0\)

\(5.0 \times 10^{9}\;\text{A/m}^2\)

\(B_0\)

18.14 T

Characteristic field

\(\alpha\)

0.902

Field exponent

\(T_c\)

92 K

Validation against Stellaris Table 8: \(B = 20\,\text{T} \rightarrow J_c \approx 2450\;\text{A/mm}^2\), \(B = 25\,\text{T} \rightarrow J_c \approx 2200\;\text{A/mm}^2\).

Parameter

Value

Description

\(T_{\text{op}}\)

20 K

\(\eta\)

\(I_{\text{lead,max}}\)

\(f_{\text{WP}}\)

1.3

Winding-pack self-field enhancement factor

Algorithm for each coil \(i\):

  1. Required ampere-turns at reactor scale:

    \[NI_i = I_{\text{device},i} \times B_{\text{scale}} \times L_{\text{scale}}\]

    where \(I_{\text{device},i}\) is the simsopt single-turn current. If per-coil currents are unavailable, \(I\) is estimated from the force data: \(I \approx (F/L) / B_{\text{device}}\).

  2. Peak conductor field estimate:

    \[B_{\text{ext},i} = \frac{(F/L)_{\text{device},i}}{I_{\text{device},i}} \times B_{\text{scale}}, \qquad B_{\text{peak},i} = f_{\text{WP}} \times B_{\text{ext},i}\]

    The factor \(f_{\text{WP}} = 1.3\) accounts for the additional self-field produced by the multi-turn winding pack at its inner edge.

  3. Critical current of the HTS cable:

    \[I_{c,\text{cable}} = J_c(B_{\text{peak}},\; T_{\text{op}}) \times A_{\text{HTS}}\]

  4. Operating current per turn (lead- or tape-limited):

    \[I_{\text{turn}} = \min\!\bigl(I_{\text{lead,max}},\; \eta \times I_{c,\text{cable}}\bigr)\]

  5. Number of turns from \(J_c\) requirements:

    \[N_{\text{turns},\,i}^{(J_c)} = \left\lceil \frac{NI_i}{I_{\text{turn},i}} \right\rceil\]

Hard constraint. The final \(N_{\text{turns},i}\) (element-wise maximum of force and \(J_c\) requirements) must satisfy \(\max_i N_{\text{turns},\,i} \leq 500\).

3. Finite-build (winding-pack) extent

With each turn occupying \(A_{\text{turn}} = 20\;\text{mm} \times 20\;\text{mm} = 400\;\text{mm}^2\) (Table 7 of Lion et al.: this area includes the REBCO tape stack, copper stabiliser, solder, steel jacket, and helium cooling channel), a square winding pack with \(N\) turns has side length

\[w_{\text{WP}} = \sqrt{N_{\text{turns}}} \times 20\;\text{mm}\]

Validation against Stellaris Table 8:

  • Coil 0: \(N = 324 \;\Rightarrow\; w = 18 \times 20\;\text{mm} = 360\;\text{mm} \;\checkmark\)

  • Coil 5: \(N = 225 \;\Rightarrow\; w = 15 \times 20\;\text{mm} = 300\;\text{mm} \;\checkmark\)

The leaderboard reports \(w_{\text{WP}}\) — the maximum winding-pack side length across all coils (in metres). This gives the finite-build extent that must be accommodated by the coil-surface and coil-coil separation gaps.

4. Finite-build coil-coil intersection check

simsopt’s CurveCurveDistance penalty measures the centreline-to-centreline distance between coil filaments. Once the winding-pack extent is known, we can check whether the finite-build coils would physically overlap.

Each coil’s winding pack extends \(w_i / 2\) from the centreline in every direction. For two coils i and j separated by centreline distance \(d_{ij}\), the clearance between their outer edges is

\[\text{clearance}_{ij} = d_{ij} - \frac{w_i}{2} - \frac{w_j}{2}\]

Because we only store the global minimum coil-coil distance \(d_{\text{cc,min}} = \min_{i<j} d_{ij}\), the most conservative check uses the largest winding-pack width for both coils:

\[\text{clearance} = d_{\text{cc,min}} - w_{\text{WP,max}}\]

where \(w_{\text{WP,max}} = \max_i w_{\text{WP},i}\). This is a hard constraint: if the clearance is negative (\(d_{\text{cc,min}} < w_{\text{WP,max}}\)), the winding packs would intersect and the design is infeasible (score = 0).

5. Per-turn force and torque

Once \(N_{\text{turns},i}\) is known for each coil, the engineering-relevant structural loads are the per-turn quantities:

\[F_{\text{turn},i} = \frac{F_{\text{reactor},i}}{N_{\text{turns},i}}, \qquad \tau_{\text{turn},i} = \frac{\tau_{\text{reactor},i}}{N_{\text{turns},i}}\]

The leaderboard reports:

  • \(F_{\text{turn}}\) — \(\max_i F_{\text{turn},i}\) (MN/m), the maximum per-turn force across all coils.

  • \(\tau_{\text{turn}}\) — \(\max_i \tau_{\text{turn},i}\) (MN), the maximum per-turn torque across all coils.

These replace the single-turn \(F_{\max}\) and \(\tau_{\max}\) in the reactor-scale leaderboard, since the single-turn values are not physically meaningful for a multi-turn winding pack.
